items.headline: Only 3.5% of U.S. adults who drink heavily got a brief intervention from a clinician, study finds
items.summary: An RTI International study in Addiction, using national survey data from more than 139,000 U.S. adults, found nearly 69% of adults who received health care were screened for alcohol use, but only 3.5% of those drinking heavily were advised to cut back. Just 7.5% of adults with alcohol use disorder reported treatment in the past year, and women were about 48% less likely than men to receive a brief intervention. Routine visits where screening already happens are a missed chance to intervene before a use disorder develops.

items.headline: California awards more than $21 million to 112 groups for overdose prevention and treatment links
items.outlet: Office of the Governor of California
items.summary: California's Department of Health Care Services is investing more than $21 million in 112 community organizations for outreach, naloxone distribution, peer navigation, and referrals to treatment through August 31, 2027, funded by SAMHSA's State Opioid Response IV grant. The state reports the program served 28,109 patients with opioid use disorder treatment from September 2024 to September 2025, including 14,090 who newly started MOUD. The awards extend the state's use of community groups as front doors to medication treatment.

items.headline: Missouri programs combine addiction, psychiatric, and pregnancy care to prevent maternal deaths
items.summary: Missouri's Pregnancy-Associated Mortality Review Board found that seven of the 108 pregnancy-related deaths from 2019 to 2023 were attributed to substance use disorder, and all were considered preventable. New efforts include Kansas City's EMBER program, which brings obstetric care into an addiction and psychiatric setting, St. Louis's BRAVE telehealth program, and a peer recovery pilot called Project STORK. Board members cite cases where clinicians changed MOUD regimens before an overdose, a reminder to keep effective treatment in place through pregnancy.

items.headline: Franklin County, Massachusetts, wins nearly $10 million for rural addiction care and jail MOUD
items.summary: The Opioid Task Force of Franklin County and the North Quabbin Region received about $6.2 million from two four-year federal grants, HRSA's Rural Communities Opioid Response Program and the First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act program, to fund rural outreach, overdose response, and naloxone distribution and training. The Franklin County Sheriff's Office received a separate five-year, $3.75 million grant to expand MOUD in the county jail and coordinate care after release. Linking jail-based MOUD to community follow-up targets the high-risk period right after incarceration.

items.headline: Iowa directs $775,550 in settlement funds to cut post-surgical opioid prescribing at eight hospitals
items.summary: Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird announced a two-year, $775,550 grant from the office's opioid settlement fund to expand the Billion Pill Pledge, a Goldfinch Health program, to eight more Iowa hospitals. The program supports best-practice surgical protocols, non-opioid pain management, patient preparation kits, and nurse support before and after surgery, and Goldfinch says the program has cut the need for opioid refills by more than 80%. The grant shows settlement dollars going to prevention at the point where many patients are first exposed to opioids.
